newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Dow, rate fears weigh on Brussels bourse.
newsitem.headline: Dow, rate fears weigh on Brussels bourse.

text.p: Belgian shares had another sad day on Friday, suffering from Dow Jones jitters and reemerging European interest rate worries, dealers said.
"Interest fears in Europe have pushed European bourses down and the volatility of the U.S. market has not exactly helped the Bel-20," a trader said.
The Bel-20 share index ended down 0.82 percent or 15.21 points to 1,847.77 with a healthy volume of 2.86 billion francs worth of Belgian shares traded.
One dealer said some investors had worried earlier in the session that the EMU stability pact being discussed at the EU summit in Dublin might fall through.
EU diplomats said after the close a deal on the stability pact had been struck. No details were immediately available.
Dealers said the end of the two-week account had also been weighing on shares. Many investors had also started settling end-of-year accounts, one said.
Financials suffered heavily in today's trade on worries over interest rates in the near future and on slipping Bunds.
"Banks and insurance companies dropped more than others because of bonds," said on trader.

Generale Bank fell two percent to 11,300 francs and insurer Fortis AG was down 1.3 percent to 4,740 francs. Bank BBL was among the biggest losers with a 2.9 percent dive to 6,310 francs. "BBL suffered from the expiry of its put warrant," a dealer said.
Another said the index would not return to its recent record levels before the year-end even if there was no major correction in the U.S.
"It's the end of the year and people have had a good run this year, so now they take profits when interest rate worries started again," he said.
Another trader expected the Bel-20 to stay between 1,820 and 1,870 before the year-end.
